summary: Round 31 recheck, 02:13-02:55Z 29 Sep. I made no Kaggle API calls and used no browser. The LB data comes from the E10 loop's 02:14Z snapshot. Before choosing, I checked all 87 earlier recheck-old items (rounds 2-30), knobarms_28sep and ideas_29sep: every live x138 knob, including the gap and ILP ones, is already covered. So I took three items whose verdict rests on the new facts (tie rule / public-private split, 12 h limit, the CI class). (A) v3 C02 rank arithmetic: the premise 'the x138 block straddles both medal cutoffs' is OVERTURNED. At 02:14Z silver ~#199 is in the 0.957 block, bronze ~#398 is in the 0.955 block, and x138 sits at ranks 568-973. The shoulder grew ~5.5 teams/h against a modelled 1.4-2.5/h. A re-run of the mc26 finals model with this field and V_pub = exp87a keeps the pair ORDER: a K-free partner (#37 or exp75) is at least as good as the best+neighbour pair (exp85a), and exp75 equals #37 under the R28 CI prior. The levels drop 0.02-0.05, card v5's П2 range is ~0.1 too high, and the ticked {#37,#38} falls to bronze ~0.38 (0.20-0.58) / silver ~0.07. The card needs a number refresh at 12:03Z; no rule changes. (B) v3 (g)6 final-days queue-growth risk is largely OVERTURNED. L is flat over 26-28 Sep (non-CI 6.9-7.8 h, CI 9.27-9.48 h, no time-of-day effect). The residual is handled by the existing rules; add one card line if the night reads come > 0.5 h slower than their parents. (C) I-045 (georgexue666 precision localiser): the class is revived on public by CI (two LB '+'), but the item stays closed: no code, runtime (CI already at 9.3-9.5 h of 12 h), and no slot or time. Side note: running tools/runtime_ledger.py --print regenerated experiments/lb_poll/ledger.md, a deterministic file the poller rewrites every 10 min that was already modified. Nothing else outside round31 was written.

findings.what: v3 C02 'rank-aware finals rule' (s_merge.json C02; FINAL_REPORT (f) and (g)5 'the plan optimises sign relative to the x138 block'). OLD VERDICT/EVIDENCE: 25 Sep LB: 241 teams at exactly 0.953, 165 >= 0.954, 3,899 teams; 'silver ~#195 and bronze ~#390 both fall INSIDE the 0.953 block, so any F1 with private > x138 by epsilon jumps ~240 places'. The rival MC (mc20 -> mc26; field of 28 Sep 13:18Z; shoulder growth 2.3/h x r U(0.6,1.1)) was built on that frame. WHAT CHANGED: (1) LB 29 Sep 02:14Z (3,979 teams): >=0.960 115; 0.959 21 (us #132, 17th of 21); 0.958 20; 0.957 49 (ranks 157-205); 0.956 115 (206-320); 0.955 111 (321-431); 0.954 136 (432-567); 0.953 406 (568-973). Silver (~#199) now sits inside the 0.957 block and bronze (~#398) inside the 0.955 block; the x138 block starts ~170 ranks below bronze. (2) The field grew in a different shape than modelled: 0.955-0.959 grew ~5.5 teams/h from 13:18Z to 02:14Z (model 1.4-2.5/h), while the 0.953 block shrank by 14 (model +1.9/h x r). Teams moved up from x138 into the shoulder (743929 knob disclosure), not new copies. (3) Tie rule (earlier submission wins) is confirmed; none of our candidate finals is byte-identical to a public file, so it only moves rival copy blocks. MC RE-RUN (mc26 unchanged apart from field, HOURS 21.75, observed rates, VPUB = exp87a, 6 scenarios): CI prior 0.0005/0.0008: {exp87a,exp75} bronze .70-.85 (base .78) / silver .48-.68; {exp87a,#37} .65-.83 (base .74) / .43-.64; {exp87a,exp85a} .61-.77 / .43-.64; ticked {#37,#38} .20-.58 (base .38) / .02-.16 (base .07). With the R28 revised CI prior (0.0002, sd 0.0010-0.0015), exp75 and #37 are equal partners (base .71-.72 bronze), and exp85a is never better. NEW VERDICT: the C02 PREMISE is OVERTURNED. 'Beat x138 by epsilon' no longer earns a medal; the relevant rivals are the 0.955-0.957 shoulder, which is largely x138 + disclosed knobs. The C02/partner CONCLUSION is UPHELD and gets stronger. In the world where the disclosed knobs are public overfit, the shoulder falls back toward x138, and a K-free partner (#37 / exp75) is the file that stays above it. The best+neighbour pair {exp87a, exp85a} stays last. The levels fall ~0.02-0.05. The currently ticked pair falls the most (bronze ~0.38 at base vs ~0.49), so leaving the ticks unchanged now costs ~0.33 bronze / ~0.45 silver (model).

findings.what: v3 FINAL_REPORT (g)6 'Kaggle queue growth near the deadline (latency may exceed 10 h on 28-29 Sep); mitigation: consolidate by 28 Sep 12:00, emergency repeat until 29 Sep 02:00'. This is the premise behind keeping the 29 Sep morning slots narrow: A-M1 (CI) by 08:45Z and M2 (non-CI) by 11:30Z. OLD EVIDENCE: a guess ('догадка'), no latency series yet. WHAT CHANGED: the ledger now has 17 COMPLETE x138-family rows. safetail non-CI L: #37 (26 Sep 00:02Z) (7.36,7.54]; exp70a/e/d (26 Sep ~21:15Z) 6.87-7.42; exp70j/k (27 Sep 05:28Z) (7.56,7.74]; exp70g (27 Sep 11:15Z) (7.49,7.67]; exp70q (27 Sep 14:37Z) (7.64,7.81]; exp78b/78a (28 Sep 00:06/00:50Z) (7.27,7.45]/(6.87,7.04]; exp85a (28 Sep 05:02Z) (7.01,7.19]. CI: exp79a (28 Sep 00:06Z) (9.27,9.45]; exp87a (28 Sep 12:14Z) (9.30,9.48]. There is no upward trend over 26-28 Sep and no time-of-day effect, even on 28 Sep, when the shoulder grew fastest. The 12 h limit keeps ~2.5 h of headroom on CI files and ~4.5 h on non-CI files. NEW VERDICT: the risk is largely OVERTURNED. The morning cutoffs are sound: exp89l submitted at ~08:00-08:45Z reads by ~17:30-18:15Z, and a non-CI M2 at 09:30-11:30Z reads by ~16:45-18:45Z. One residual remains. A final-day slowdown would show first in the night reads (exp89p due ~07:40-08:00Z, exp89r/exp75 ~09:25-09:35Z). A growth of more than ~0.7 h pushes exp89p past the 08:40Z A-M1 header, and the existing rule then already codes P '?' -> A-M1 UNUSED. A growth of more than ~1.3 h makes an 11:30Z M2 read land after the 20:00Z tick. That is harmless, because an unread file is never a final, but the user should know.

findings.what: I-045, v3 FINAL_REPORT (i) 'Прецизионный детектор pool-2 (georgexue666): нет кода модели, нет D1.json, нет счёта LB' (s_merge dropped kaggle-intel/precision-detector-localiser). OLD VERDICT: both lenses REFUTED. VALUE: 7 um matching barely reacts to sub-2 um moves (none 132,366 vs head 132,326 matches). A Kaggle-GT-trained localiser failed embryo-held-out (retrained V1284 was 12% worse on 44b6, z bias -0.54 um), so the move 'cannot transfer'. SCHEDULE: no model code, no lab replay, and an untimed extra UNet pass under x138's timer. WHAT CHANGED: CI (I-324, yuki0731 coord-inject) is the same class: GT-trained refiners snap existing final nodes within 3 um. It read '+' on the LB twice: probe 48 +0.001 (UP 33) and probe 51 0.959 vs 0.958 (UP 12). Both are out-of-embryo reads. The 12 h limit was also clarified: CI costs ~+2.2 h of hidden-run time (7.0-7.2 -> 9.3-9.5 h). NEW VERDICT: the CLASS verdict is OVERTURNED on the public embryo, so the value and transfer objections were wrong in sign there. The ITEM stays CLOSED for four reasons that still hold. (a) There is still no known inference code (not re-checked on Kaggle, to save API load). (b) A pool-2 UNet pass is heavier than one CI detector pass, and CI files already sit at 9.3-9.5 h against the 12 h limit. A second localiser pass would push L to ~11.5 h+, into the timer and insertion-gate zone. (c) A new mechanism after 02:00Z would need build + dummy + the user's yes, plus a ~10-11.5 h read, all before the 20:00Z tick. That is not reachable with the 2 remaining slots, which MORNING TABLE v1.1 already assigns. (d) CI already takes the node-placement headroom that I-045 was after. The transfer objection (Kaggle-GT localisers can fail across embryos through the z convention) was already weighed for CI in R25-RC-C/R28-RC-C. This recheck adds nothing to CI's private prior.
